name: ml-acceleration.md
html:
ML Acceleration — ONNX Runtime Web, WebNN & WASM

The site's machine-learning layer. Every model is a tiny ONNX graph generated at build time (shared/scripts/build/gen-onnx-models.mjs) and executed lazily through ONNX Runtime Web — never on the critical path, always with a deterministic fallback.

Execution-provider ladder

flowchart TD A["runMlModel(slug, feeds)"] --> B{"navigator.ml?"} B -->|"yes"| C["webnn EP — NPU"] B -->|"no"| D["skip webnn"] C --> E{"navigator.gpu?"} D --> E E -->|"yes"| F["webgpu EP — shared GPU"] E -->|"no"| G["skip webgpu"] F --> H["wasm EP — SIMD fallback"] G --> H H -->|"create fails"| I["retry wasm-only"] I -->|"still fails"| J["null → caller's heuristic"]

core/utils/ml/ort-engine.ts owns the runtime:

  • Lazy by contract — import('onnxruntime-web/webgpu') runs on the first inference call, so the ~1MB runtime bundle and the wasm binaries in /ort/ never touch TTI/LCP.
  • Sessions cache by slug — /models/<slug>.onnx is fetched and compiled once per page lifetime; concurrent callers share the same promise.
  • EP probing, not hoping — webnn is requested only when navigator.ml exists, webgpu only when navigator.gpu exists. A rejected accelerated session retries wasm-only before returning null.
  • Every failure → null — callers keep their exact pre-ML heuristic, so a missing model, absent runtime, or dead driver can never break a feature.

The models

ModelInputOutputConsumer
intent[hoverNorm, speedNorm, bias]sigmoid → P(navigate)npu-predict prefetch scorer
frametime[5-frame window, quality]predicted frame ms/100star-field + earth adaptive pixel-ratio
superres-2x[1,3,H,W] RGBA planar[1,3,2H,2W]media-figure ladder end
diagram-cost[nodes, edges, nesting, self]predicted render msdocs mermaid scheduling

intent — navigation prefetch scorer

core/utils/gpu/npu-predict.ts ran a hand-tuned linear blend (base + hover·w + (1−speed)·w) for years. The intent model lifts those same weights into logit space (sigmoid(2.2·hover − 1.6·speed − 0.6)) so the NPU tier now executes a real graph — on an actual NPU when the machine has one — while every lower tier computes a comparable score. A null inference falls back to the original blend.

frametime — three.js adaptive quality

core/utils/ml/frame-time.ts keeps a zero-allocation ring of the last five frame times (normalized /100ms) plus the current quality level. Every 30 frames it fires one inference — never awaited inside the rAF tick — and steps the pixel-ratio multiplier:

  • predicted > 17ms → quality −0.15 (floor 0.5)
  • predicted < 12ms → quality +0.05 (ceiling 1.0)

Star-field (tickStar) and earth (tickEarth) record each frame and re-apply setPixelRatio only on a transition — the DLSS-style contract of "render smaller when the model predicts overrun, recover when it sees headroom". This is the honest version of console-grade quality: the browser can't fake PS5 silicon, but prediction-driven resolution scaling is the same technique consoles use for dynamic resolution.

superres-2x — low-quality media enhancement

When the manifest's quality ladder ends on a rung that still under-resolves the display box (naturalWidth < displayWidth), the figure runs the Conv+DepthToSpace model — 3 channels × 4 subpixel phases of separable Catmull-Rom bicubic taps — producing a 2× ImageBitmap that re-uploads into the same GPU texture via processBitmapGPU. Same painted box, sharper bitmap, no layout shift, no blink. Inputs cap at 512² px (the readback marshals on the main thread); larger media already has the quality it needs.

Media pipeline: warm → decode → enhance

flowchart LR W["warmObserver — 600px margin"] -->|"first rung only"| F["detached fetch — CDN edge + HTTP cache hot"] O["imgObserver — 100px margin"] --> L["ladder climb — serial ascending rungs"] F -.->|"force-cache replay"| L L --> D["decodeImageWASM — worker createImageBitmap + GPU resize hints"] D -->|"bitmap"| U["processBitmapGPU — zero-copy VRAM upload"] D -->|"null"| T["processTextureGPU — img element fallback"] U --> S{"under-resolved?"} T --> S S -->|"yes"| SR["superres-2x → processBitmapGPU"] S -->|"no"| Z["done"]
  • Warm band: a second IntersectionObserver at 600px fires one detached fetch of the first ladder rung — only the entry rung, since the climb ascends serially and warming the top rung would fight the low rung for bandwidth on media that may never publish.
  • WASM decode: at ladder end, wasmImageDecoder.decodeImageWASM replays the confirmed URL through fetch(cache: 'force-cache') (the warm + climb already paid the network cost), decodes in a wasm-pool worker via createImageBitmap with GPU resize hints, and uploads the bitmap zero-copy. A null result falls back to the classic processTextureGPU(img) upload.
  • Enhance last: super-resolution consumes the decoded bitmap when present (its width is the true pixel count) else the <img> — the enhancement is opportunistic and never blocks the climb.

diagram-cost — mermaid scheduling

The docs viewer's mermaid blocks render through rust/diagram (wasm). Before each block renders, four cheap regex counts (nodes, edges, subgraph nesting, self-messages) feed the diagram-cost model; a prediction over 24ms yields one task turn first, so a large graph can't long-task the docs view between blocks. Small diagrams render immediately as before.

Artifacts & delivery

flowchart LR G["gen-onnx-models.mjs"] --> M["website/public/models/*.onnx — ~3KB each"] G --> O["website/public/ort/ort-wasm-*.wasm — ORT runtime binaries"] M --> V["vite publicDir copy → dist/"] O --> V V --> I["immutable-cacheable — fetched on first inference only"]
  • gen-onnx-models.mjs serializes the graphs by hand (minimal protobuf writer — no external model toolchain, no network) and is invoked by build-targets.mjs before build 0 copies public/.
  • ORT wasm binaries are copied from node_modules/onnxruntime-web/dist — the asyncify build for jsep EPs (WebNN/WebGPU) plus the plain simd-threaded build for the wasm EP. Committed artifacts, same convention as /wasm/*/.
  • ort.env.wasm.wasmPaths = '/ort/' — ORT fetches the exact binary its chosen EP needs; untouched paths are never downloaded.
  • env.wasm.numThreads = 1 — the models are sub-millisecond; the proxy worker isn't worth a thread slot.

Failure contract

Every public surface resolves null/quality-hold/heuristic on any failure — import, session create (both EP attempts), session.run, bad output shape. The ML layer can only ever improve on the baseline behavior it replaced; it can never regress it. Jest routes onnxruntime-web through shared/tests/__mocks__/onnxruntime-web.js so suites drive every arm deterministically.
